newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling gains further against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling gains further against dollar.

text.p: High exporter sales helped strengthen the Kenyan shilling on Thursday in a moderately active market, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 55.70 against the dollar from 55.74 on Wednesday. On the pound, the shilling was posted weaker at 90.91 from 89.79.
"Exporter sales saw the shilling strengthen against the dollar to close at 55.65/75 as compared to the opening levels of 55.70/80," one commercial dealer said.
Another dealer said the exchange rate appreciated slightly with supply exceeding demand. A leading dealer said he expected shilling firmness to persist in the short-term.
Dealers said the market was moderately active as industrial and oil importers came into the market looking for dollars -- pushing the dollar up slightly temporarily.
"The situation was only temporary as the demand for dollars was completely satisfied by inflows of dollars from exporters," one dealer said.
Dealers said the downward trend of the dollar was expected to continue for the rest of the week in the absence of intervention by the central bank.
The money market was a bit tight as many banks invested in treasury bills. Rates remained at 20 percent levels.
